userStories.title: Budget create, update, delete and resume are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record committed budget management actions atomically through both admin and project route prefixes, without duplicating approval-decide auditing.

**Motivation** — A budget raised, a schedule edited, a runner disabled or a repo removed leaves only a `FleetActivity` row, which the Audit log (`GET /api/audit`) does not show.

**Approach** — Relevant design notes, verbatim:
- **Record next to the activity row.** Every admin write in this feature except the knowledge routes already calls `FleetActivityService.record` inside its `txManager.run`. It records its entry inside that same callback, right after the activity row, so the two commit or roll back together.
- **`resume` records only on the budget routes.** `BudgetsService.resume` records `fleet.budget.resume` only when `opts.approvalId` is absent. A `raise_budget_and_resume` decide calls `resume` with `opts.approvalId` inside its own transaction, and its `fleet.approval.decide.budget` entry (audit-fleet-routes) covers that write.
- **Only the action is recorded, not its follow-ons in the same transaction.** Deleting a paused budget closes its pending approval (`ApprovalCloser.closeForPolicy`) and a budget resume from the budgets page closes it as `manual_resume`. Both happen in the action's own transaction, so they are covered by the action's entry, as audit-core's rule says.
- **`projectId` is the row's project.** A budget's `projectId` (`null` for a global or runner policy), a schedule's, a repo's and a config job's project, a rerun job's project. Runners and enrollments have no project (`null`). An analytics delete has the query's `projectId`, `null` for a delete across every project.

Writer changes, verbatim:
| Service.method | Today | Change |
| `BudgetsService.create` | `txManager.run`, `budgets.service.ts:59` | `record` inside, after `this.record` (the activity row) |
| `BudgetsService.update` | `txManager.run`, `:77` | `record` inside, after the activity row |
| `BudgetsService.remove` | `txManager.run`, `:98` | `record` inside, after the activity row; the summary reads `policy.pausedAt` from the locked row |
| `BudgetsService.resume` | `txManager.run`, `:116` | `record` inside, after the activity row, only when `opts.approvalId` is absent |

Contract rows, verbatim (Write | Key | resourceType | resourceId | projectId | summary):
| budget create | `fleet.budget.create` | `fleet-budget` | policy id | policy's `projectId` | `created <scopeType> policy` (`global`, `runner`, `project`, `repo`) |
| budget update | `fleet.budget.update` | `fleet-budget` | policy id | policy's `projectId` | `fieldsSummary(dto)`, e.g. `fields: amountUsd, hardStop` |
| budget delete | `fleet.budget.delete` | `fleet-budget` | policy id | policy's `projectId` | `deleted`, or `deleted while paused` when the policy had `pausedAt` |
| budget resume (route) | `fleet.budget.resume` | `fleet-budget` | policy id | policy's `projectId` | `resumed` |

`fieldsSummary` is `src/audit/audit-summary.ts`: it lists the sorted names of the defined fields and never their values.

**Scope** — In: inject required AuditRecorder as the last BudgetsService constructor parameter; await record after activity in its existing four transactions; create the budget audit integration suite and direct resume unit tests. Preserve responses, the evaluator signal and approval closes. Out: schedule writers (US-002), runner/repo writers (US-003), config/knowledge writers (US-004), ingest/analytics writers (US-005). Recording `BudgetsService.resume` when `ApprovalsService.decide` calls it with `opts.approvalId` is out of scope; the decide's `fleet.approval.decide.budget` entry covers it. Recording the approval close that a budget delete or a budget-page resume commits in its own transaction is out of scope; the action's own entry covers that transaction. ACs for the `runner` and `repo` budget scopes and for budget update and resume through the admin prefix are out of scope; the contract table defines their summaries, and the project-prefix ACs exercise the same `BudgetsService` methods.

**Interface** — Read-only spec contracts: `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)`, `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }`; `fieldsSummary(patch)`. Existing TypeScript input shape to consume, not redefine:
```typescript
export interface AuditRecordInput {
  key: string;
  resourceType: string;
  resourceId: string;
  projectId?: string | null;
  summary?: string;
}
```

Verification uses the real HTTP routes and stored entries, including the seam `POST /api/fleet/approvals/:id/decide` → `ApprovalsService.decide` → `BudgetsService.resume(…, { approvalId })`. Clear budget approvals and every BudgetPolicy before each AC because scope/window is unique. Create paused policies and pending approvals as described in the shared analysis; restore rejection spies. Required refusal behavior is no audit entry on pre-write errors; record rejection rolls the transaction back and propagates an error status.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] When root POSTs /api/fleet/budgets with a global policy, the 201 result leaves exactly one AuditEntry for the new policy id with key fleet.budget.create, resourceType fleet-budget, projectId null, actorType USER, actorId root's id, origin rest and summary created global policy.

[integration] When root POSTs /api/projects/web/fleet/budgets with a project policy, exactly one AuditEntry for the new policy id has key fleet.budget.create, projectId web's id and summary created project policy.

[integration] When two POST /api/projects/web/fleet/budgets calls target the same project scope and window, their 201 then 409 fleet.budgets outcomes increase fleet.budget.create entries with projectId web's id by exactly one across both calls.
[integration] When dev, who has no budget key, POSTs /api/projects/web/fleet/budgets, the 403 refusal leaves no fleet.budget.create AuditEntry with actorId dev's id.

[integration] When POST /api/projects/web/fleet/budgets runs while app.get(AuditRecorder).record is spied to reject, its error-status outcome rolls back the transaction, leaving no BudgetPolicy row with projectId web's id and no AuditEntry for the failed creation.

[integration] When PATCH /api/projects/web/fleet/budgets/:id receives { amountUsd: 30, hardStop: false }, exactly one AuditEntry for the policy has key fleet.budget.update and summary fields: amountUsd, hardStop.

[integration] When DELETE /api/projects/web/fleet/budgets/:id removes a policy that is not paused, the 204 outcome leaves exactly one AuditEntry for the policy with key fleet.budget.delete and summary deleted.

[integration] When DELETE /api/fleet/budgets/:id removes a global policy inserted directly with a pausedAt, exactly one AuditEntry for the policy has key fleet.budget.delete, projectId null and summary deleted while paused.

[integration] When POST /api/projects/web/fleet/budgets/:id/resume receives an amountUsd above the window's spend for a paused policy, the 200 outcome leaves exactly one AuditEntry for the policy with key fleet.budget.resume and summary resumed.
[integration] When POST /api/projects/web/fleet/budgets/:id/resume targets a policy that is not paused, the 409 fleet.budgetNotPaused outcome leaves no fleet.budget.resume AuditEntry for the policy.

[integration] When POST /api/fleet/approvals/:id/decide receives { decision: 'raise_budget_and_resume', amountUsd } for the pending approval of a paused policy, the 200 outcome leaves no fleet.budget.resume AuditEntry for that policy.

[unit] When BudgetsService.resume runs with stub collaborators, a stub transaction manager whose run calls its callback, a stub recorder and opts.approvalId a1, it does not call the recorder's record; the same call without opts calls record once with key fleet.budget.resume.

routing.reasoning: Standard recorder integration in one service plus two test files, with a nested approval-resume seam and atomic rollback; strict isolated TDD is required for permission-gated admin audit behavior.

modifiedFiles.reason: injects AuditRecorder as the last constructor parameter and records inside create's, update's, remove's and resume's transactions after the activity row (resume only when opts.approvalId is absent); responses, the evaluator signal and the approval closes are unchanged.

userStories.title: Schedule create, update, enable, disable and delete are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record the five committed schedule management actions with project/actor attribution and omit unchanged enable/disable operations.

**Motivation** — A budget raised, a schedule edited, a runner disabled or a repo removed leaves only a `FleetActivity` row, which the Audit log (`GET /api/audit`) does not show.

**Approach** — Relevant design notes, verbatim:
- **Record next to the activity row.** Every admin write in this feature except the knowledge routes already calls `FleetActivityService.record` inside its `txManager.run`. It records its entry inside that same callback, right after the activity row, so the two commit or roll back together.
- **The key is the route's `@Requires` key.** Schedule enable and disable record `fleet.schedule.update` (the key both routes require), told apart by summary. Config edit and regenerate record `fleet.job.config.edit`, and the drift check records `fleet.repo.drift.check`.
- **Only committed writes are recorded.** A refused request (401, 403, 404, 409, 400) records nothing. So does a write that finds nothing to do:
  - an `enable` of a schedule that is already enabled, or a `disable` of one already disabled (both return the row unchanged);
  - an ingest re-queue that queues no row (`queued: 0`);
  - an analytics delete that deletes no row and marks no ingest row (every count in `DeletedCounts` is 0).

Writer changes, verbatim:
| `SchedulesService.create`, `update`, `remove` | `txManager.run`, `schedules.service.ts:92`, `:107`, `:134` | `record` inside, after the activity row |
| `SchedulesService.enable`, `disable` | `txManager.run`, `:144`, `:165` | `record` inside, after the activity row; not on the early `return current` |

Contract rows, verbatim (Write | Key | resourceType | resourceId | projectId | summary):
| schedule create | `fleet.schedule.create` | `fleet-schedule` | schedule id | schedule's project | `created on repo <repoId>` |
| schedule update | `fleet.schedule.update` | `fleet-schedule` | schedule id | schedule's project | `fieldsSummary(dto)`, e.g. `fields: cron, timezone` |
| schedule enable | `fleet.schedule.update` | `fleet-schedule` | schedule id | schedule's project | `enabled` |
| schedule disable | `fleet.schedule.update` | `fleet-schedule` | schedule id | schedule's project | `disabled` |
| schedule delete | `fleet.schedule.delete` | `fleet-schedule` | schedule id | schedule's project | `deleted` |

`fieldsSummary` is `src/audit/audit-summary.ts`: it lists the sorted names of the defined fields and never their values. `<repoId>` and `<provider>` are the stored repo's id and provider. The table never lists a value from a request body other than field names.

**Scope** — In: add required AuditRecorder last in SchedulesService; await record after each activity call in the five transactions; update schedules.service.spec.ts's direct constructor with mockAuditRecorder and keep existing assertions; create the schedule audit integration suite. Out: budgets (US-001), runners/repos/enrollments (US-003), config/knowledge (US-004), ingest/analytics (US-005). The key a scheduled fire records under and the closes a bash or assistant decide commits before its 409 are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-system`). Preserve existing lock ordering, row ownership/permission checks, enable owner-access validation and responses.

**Interface** — Read-only spec contracts: `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)`, `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }`; `fieldsSummary(patch)`. Existing TypeScript signatures to consume, not redefine:
```typescript
record(input: AuditRecordInput): Promise<void>
fieldsSummary(patch: object): string | undefined
```

Verification must enter the HTTP routes through bootHttpApp/AppModule and inspect stored AuditEntry rows. Use a fresh fixture name for rollback. Add a second developer through the user/member routes, with resetThrottle before login. Keep AC8-10 in the same describe after AC7 so they exercise the same disabled/enabled schedule. Give the nonowner-refusal AC its own schedule without a prior update entry, rather than reusing the owner-update AC's already-audited schedule. A refusal (including another developer's 403 permissions) records nothing; an awaited record rejection rolls back the schedule and activity and propagates an error status.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] When dev POSTs /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules with a valid template on web's repo, the 201 outcome leaves exactly one AuditEntry for the new schedule id with key fleet.schedule.create, resourceType fleet-schedule, projectId web's id, actorType USER, actorId dev's id, origin rest and summary created on repo <repoId>.
[integration] When POST /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules uses name secret-name, the resulting fleet.schedule.create AuditEntry summary does not include secret-name.
[integration] When viewer POSTs /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules, the 403 refusal leaves no fleet.schedule.create AuditEntry with actorId viewer's id.

[integration] When POST /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules runs while app.get(AuditRecorder).record is spied to reject, the error-status outcome rolls back the transaction, leaving no JobSchedule row with that name and no AuditEntry for the failed creation.

[integration] When the schedule's owner PATCHes /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules/:id with { cron: '0 6 * * *', timezone: 'UTC' }, exactly one AuditEntry for the schedule has key fleet.schedule.update and summary fields: cron, timezone.

[integration] When a second developer who does not own the schedule PATCHes /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules/:id, the 403 permissions refusal leaves no fleet.schedule.update AuditEntry for the schedule.

[integration] When POST /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules/:id/disable targets an enabled schedule, the 200 outcome leaves exactly one AuditEntry for the schedule with key fleet.schedule.update and summary disabled.

[integration] When POST /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules/:id/disable is repeated on that disabled schedule, the 200 outcome leaves still exactly one AuditEntry for the schedule with summary disabled, returning the row unchanged.

[integration] When its owner POSTs /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules/:id/enable for that disabled schedule, the 200 outcome leaves exactly one AuditEntry for the schedule with key fleet.schedule.update and summary enabled.

[integration] When POST /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules/:id/enable is repeated on that enabled schedule, the 200 outcome leaves still exactly one AuditEntry for the schedule with summary enabled, returning the row unchanged.

[integration] When the schedule's owner DELETEs /api/projects/web/fleet/schedules/:id, the 204 outcome leaves exactly one AuditEntry for the schedule with key fleet.schedule.delete and summary deleted.

routing.reasoning: Additive instrumentation of five existing transactions and a direct-constructor test update; own-row authorization and permission-gated admin actions require strict isolated TDD.

userStories.title: Enrollment create, runner update and delete, repo create and delete are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit enrollment creation, runner administration and repo registration/deletion in their existing write transactions, leaving runner enrollment and repo checks unchanged.

**Motivation** — A budget raised, a schedule edited, a runner disabled or a repo removed leaves only a `FleetActivity` row, which the Audit log (`GET /api/audit`) does not show.

**Approach** — Relevant design notes, verbatim:
- **Record next to the activity row.** Every admin write in this feature except the knowledge routes already calls `FleetActivityService.record` inside its `txManager.run`. It records its entry inside that same callback, right after the activity row, so the two commit or roll back together.
- **A repo check records nothing.** `FleetReposService.check` runs the forge check and writes no row.
- **`projectId` is the row's project.** A budget's `projectId` (`null` for a global or runner policy), a schedule's, a repo's and a config job's project, a rerun job's project. Runners and enrollments have no project (`null`). An analytics delete has the query's `projectId`, `null` for a delete across every project.

Writer changes, verbatim:
| `EnrollmentService.create` | `txManager.run`, `enrollment.service.ts:34` | `record` inside, after the activity row |
| `RunnersService.update`, `remove` | `txManager.run`, `runners.service.ts:51`, `:65` | `record` inside, after the activity row |
| `FleetReposService.create`, `remove` | `txManager.run`, `fleet-repos.service.ts:38`, `:69` | `record` inside, after the activity row |

Contract rows, verbatim (Write | Key | resourceType | resourceId | projectId | summary):
| enrollment create | `fleet.enrollment.create` | `fleet-enrollment` | enrollment id | `null` | `created` |
| runner update | `fleet.runner.update` | `fleet-runner` | runner id | `null` | `fieldsSummary(clean)`, e.g. `fields: enabled` |
| runner delete | `fleet.runner.delete` | `fleet-runner` | runner id | `null` | `deleted` |
| repo create | `fleet.repo.create` | `fleet-repo` | repo id | repo's project | `registered <provider>` (`github`, `gitlab`) |
| repo delete | `fleet.repo.delete` | `fleet-repo` | repo id | repo's project | `deleted` |

`fieldsSummary` is `src/audit/audit-summary.ts`: it lists the sorted names of the defined fields and never their values. `<repoId>` and `<provider>` are the stored repo's id and provider. The table never lists a value from a request body other than field names.

**Scope** — In: add required AuditRecorder last in EnrollmentService, RunnersService and FleetReposService; await record after existing activities in the five named writes; pass mockAuditRecorder last in enrollment.service.spec.ts, runners.service.spec.ts and fleet-repos.service.spec.ts, keeping existing assertions; create the runners/repos audit integration suite. Out: budget writers (US-001), schedules (US-002), config/knowledge (US-004), ingest/analytics (US-005). The runner protocol routes (`/fleet/runner/sync` with its command acks and job reports, `/fleet/runner/enroll`, log append, bundle upload, runner tool calls) are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-system`). Keep EnrollmentService.enroll and its credentials, forge HTTP checks and existing busy/duplicate refusals unchanged. Never include labels, names, owner/name, token or hash values in summaries.

**Interface** — Read-only spec contracts: `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)`, `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }`; `fieldsSummary(patch)`. Existing TypeScript signatures to consume, not redefine:
```typescript
record(input: AuditRecordInput): Promise<void>
fieldsSummary(patch: object): string | undefined
```

Verification boots the real AppModule and sends authenticated HTTP calls. Use startFakeForge with the GitHub app environment and acme/extra installation/repo routes, restoring environment after the suite. Use a fresh runner/repo for each deletion, never the world's repo; unfinished-job fixtures are RUNNING for the runner or QUEUED for the repo. For the check AC use a directly inserted or seeded repo with no prior AuditEntry, not the repo whose HTTP registration AC7 already audited. A busy runner/repo returns 409 fleet.runnerBusy/fleet.repoBusy, a duplicate repo returns 409, and each refusal leaves no new entry. A record rejection must roll the domain and activity changes back and propagate an error status.

[integration] When dev, who has no global key, POSTs /api/fleet/enrollments, the 403 refusal leaves no fleet.enrollment.create AuditEntry with actorId dev's id.

[integration] When DELETE /api/fleet/repos/:id targets a repo with no unfinished job, the 204 outcome leaves exactly one AuditEntry for the repo with key fleet.repo.delete and summary deleted.

userStories.title: Config jobs, the knowledge patterns save and the reindex request are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit config edit/regenerate/drift dispatches and knowledge patterns/reindex actions with correct modes, rollback, and audit-before-enqueue ordering.

**Motivation** — The fleet's admin writes record none.

**Approach** — Relevant design notes, verbatim:
- **Record next to the activity row.** Every admin write in this feature except the knowledge routes already calls `FleetActivityService.record` inside its `txManager.run`. It records its entry inside that same callback, right after the activity row, so the two commit or roll back together.
- **The key is the route's `@Requires` key.** Schedule enable and disable record `fleet.schedule.update` (the key both routes require), told apart by summary. Config edit and regenerate record `fleet.job.config.edit`, and the drift check records `fleet.repo.drift.check`.
- **The knowledge patterns save wraps its write in `audited`.** `KnowledgeIndexService.savePatterns` calls `saveProjectPatterns` with no transaction. It runs that call inside `this.audit.audited(...)`.
- **The knowledge reindex records an entry with no other write.** `POST …/knowledge/repos/:repoId/reindex` only adds the repo to the in-memory `KnowledgeIndexQueue`, but it is a human's action that starts an index pass, and the inventory lists it as a write. `ProjectKnowledgeController.reindex` records `fleet.knowledge.repo.reindex` through `this.audit.audited(...)`, with a callback that writes nothing, and calls `this.queue.enqueue` after `audited` resolves. So a failed record queues no pass.

Writer changes, verbatim:
| `ConfigJobsService.create` (private, behind `submitEdit`, `submitRegenerate`, `submitDrift`) | `txManager.run`, `config-jobs.service.ts:125` | `record` inside, after the activity row; key from `mode` (`drift` → `fleet.repo.drift.check`, else `fleet.job.config.edit`) |
| `KnowledgeIndexService.savePatterns` | one `saveProjectPatterns` call, no transaction | wrap the call in `audit.audited` |
| `ProjectKnowledgeController.reindex` | `this.queue.enqueue(repo.id, 'admin')`, no write | `audit.audited` with a callback that writes nothing, then `enqueue` |

Contract rows, verbatim (Write | Key | resourceType | resourceId | projectId | summary):
| config edit | `fleet.job.config.edit` | `fleet-job` | job id | repo's project | `edit on repo <repoId>` |
| config regenerate | `fleet.job.config.edit` | `fleet-job` | job id | repo's project | `regenerate on repo <repoId>` |
| drift check | `fleet.repo.drift.check` | `fleet-job` | job id | repo's project | `drift on repo <repoId>` |
| knowledge patterns save | `fleet.knowledge.patterns.update` | `project` | project id | project id | `custom patterns`, or `default patterns` for the `null` body |
| knowledge reindex | `fleet.knowledge.repo.reindex` | `fleet-repo` | repo id | project id | `reindex queued` |

`<repoId>` and `<provider>` are the stored repo's id and provider. The table never lists a value from a request body other than field names. For the patterns route, the null case is the accepted { patterns: null } body, preserving the existing DTO and default-pattern behavior.

**Scope** — In: add required AuditRecorder last in ConfigJobsService, KnowledgeIndexService and ProjectKnowledgeController; instrument only private config dispatch create; use audited for patterns and the empty-write reindex transaction; update config-jobs.service.spec.ts, knowledge-index.service.spec.ts and project-knowledge.controller.spec.ts direct constructions with mockAuditRecorder, preserving their existing assertions; add the controller's rejecting-audited case and the config/knowledge audit integration suite. Out: budget writers (US-001), schedules (US-002), runner/repo registration management (US-003), ingest/analytics (US-005). Recording the knowledge index passes that a patterns save queues is out of scope; the passes are the index queue's (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-system`). The runner protocol routes (`/fleet/runner/sync` with its command acks and job reports, `/fleet/runner/enroll`, log append, bundle upload, runner tool calls) are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-system`). The fleet system writers (`ApprovalExpirySweeper`, `PendingActionExpirySweeper`, `BudgetSweeper`, `BundleIngestSweeper`, `KnowledgePoller`, `KnowledgeIndexQueue`, `FleetLogRetentionProcessor`, `EnrollmentRetentionProcessor`, `ScheduleTicker`, `FleetSweeper`, `FleetPrStateRefresher`, `ThreadIngestHook`) and job placement are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-system`). Runner config fetch/fencing remains unchanged. Never audit PR titles, file paths/content, patterns or their before/after values.

**Interface** — Read-only spec contracts: `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)`, `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }`. Existing TypeScript signatures to consume, not redefine:
```typescript
export type AuditEntriesOf<T> = (result: T) => AuditRecordInput | readonly AuditRecordInput[];
audited<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>, entriesOf: AuditEntriesOf<T>): Promise<T>
record(input: AuditRecordInput): Promise<void>
```

Verification enters named routes through bootHttpApp/AppModule and reads real audit rows. Use startFakeForge as fleet-repo-config-api.integration.spec.ts does; config jobs on one repo exclude each other, so directly cancel earlier jobs before cases that require no active one, but retain AC4's QUEUED drift job for AC5. Toggle FLEET_CFG.knowledgeIndexEnabled and restore it after the suite. Spy KnowledgeIndexQueue.enqueue to do nothing so no real pass starts. Use a fresh directly inserted project repo with no reindex audit entry for the disabled-reindex AC, rather than reusing the enabled-reindex AC's audited resource. Patterns-save record rejection must roll back stored patterns; reindex audited rejection must prevent enqueue. Refused actions store no entry, including 409 fleet.configJobActive and 409 knowledge.disabled; the latter queues nothing. Preserve placement, live events, 202 reindex response and all other response/status/permission contracts.

userStories.title: Ingest re-queues and the analytics delete are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit the three ingest requeues and analytics deletion only when their returned counts prove a row was queued, deleted or marked.

**Motivation** — The fleet's admin writes record none.

**Approach** — Relevant design notes, verbatim:
- **Record next to the activity row.** Every admin write in this feature except the knowledge routes already calls `FleetActivityService.record` inside its `txManager.run`. It records its entry inside that same callback, right after the activity row, so the two commit or roll back together.
- **Only committed writes are recorded.** A refused request (401, 403, 404, 409, 400) records nothing. So does a write that finds nothing to do:
  - an `enable` of a schedule that is already enabled, or a `disable` of one already disabled (both return the row unchanged);
  - an ingest re-queue that queues no row (`queued: 0`);
  - an analytics delete that deletes no row and marks no ingest row (every count in `DeletedCounts` is 0).
- **The ingest controller records in its `queue` helper.** `FleetIngestController.queue` owns the ingest transaction. It gains the entry's key, `resourceType` and summary label next to its existing `action`, `entityType` and `entityId` arguments, and records inside its `txManager.run` when `run()` returned more than 0.
- **`projectId` is the row's project.** A budget's `projectId` (`null` for a global or runner policy), a schedule's, a repo's and a config job's project, a rerun job's project. Runners and enrollments have no project (`null`). An analytics delete has the query's `projectId`, `null` for a delete across every project.

Writer changes, verbatim:
| `FleetIngestController.queue` | `txManager.run`, `fleet-ingest.controller.ts:77` | `record` inside, after the activity row, when `n > 0` |
| `AnalyticsService.deleteRows` | `txManager.run`, `analytics.service.ts:144` | `record` inside, after the activity row, when any count is above 0 |

Contract rows, verbatim (Write | Key | resourceType | resourceId | projectId | summary):
| ingest backfill | `fleet.ingest.backfill` | `fleet-ingest` | `all` | `null` | `backfill queued <n>` |
| ingest rerun of one job | `fleet.ingest.rerun` | `fleet-job` | job id | job's project | `rerun queued <n>` |
| ingest rerun of outdated rows | `fleet.ingest.rerun` | `fleet-ingest` | `all` | `null` | `rerun outdated queued <n>` |
| analytics delete | `fleet.analytics.delete` | `fleet-analytics` | query `projectId`, or `all` | query `projectId` or `null` | `deleted <costEvents> cost events, <stories> stories, <reviews> reviews, <ingestRowsMarked> ingest rows marked` |

`<n>` is the count the ingest repository method returned.

**Scope** — In: add required AuditRecorder last in FleetIngestController and AnalyticsService; extend queue metadata and add conditional awaited record calls inside existing transactions; update analytics.service.spec.ts to pass mockAuditRecorder, retain existing assertions including a single txManager.run call, and add all-zero/nonzero cases; create the ingest/analytics audit integration suite. Preserve FleetActivity writes even on zero counts, the post-commit kick, refusals and responses. Out: budget writers (US-001), schedules (US-002), runners/repos/enrollments (US-003), config/knowledge (US-004). The fleet system writers (`ApprovalExpirySweeper`, `PendingActionExpirySweeper`, `BudgetSweeper`, `BundleIngestSweeper`, `KnowledgePoller`, `KnowledgeIndexQueue`, `FleetLogRetentionProcessor`, `EnrollmentRetentionProcessor`, `ScheduleTicker`, `FleetSweeper`, `FleetPrStateRefresher`, `ThreadIngestHook`) and job placement are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-fleet-system`). Never summarize cutoff or confirmation values.

**Interface** — Read-only spec contracts: `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)`, `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }`. Changed helper contract, verbatim:
- `FleetIngestController.queue` (private) — Baseline: `queue(actorId, action, entityType, entityId, projectId, run)`. Target: it also takes the entry's `key`, `resourceType`, `resourceId` and summary label, and records when `run()` returned more than 0.
Do not wrap these existing transactions in audited.

Verification boots AppModule and invokes each named route through HTTP, then reads real AuditEntry rows. Each ingest fixture explicitly specifies status and parserVersion: insertIngestRow defaults to done/version 1, so change it to version 3 for a current rerun or 2 for outdated. Set unrelated ingest rows to pending/version 3 before count-sensitive cases. Await BundleIngestService.idle() after every queue route and before the next setup. Analytics uses a fresh insertAnalyticsJob/insertCostEvent fixture with no ingest row and no unrelated rows before the cutoff for deterministic counts. Unknown-job rerun returns 404 fleet.jobs with no entry; wrong confirmation returns 400 fleet.analyticsDelete with no entry. A record rejection rolls the queue mutation and activity back and propagates an error status. Global all entries use scoped before/after comparisons when fixture setup may have produced earlier rows. Before absolute no-entry analytics ACs, clear only the relevant prior analytics audit rows for the project/key so a previous successful delete cannot invalidate the empty baseline; retain the domain fixtures appropriate to each AC.

analysis:
FEATURE AND DISCOVERY
This is an enhancement of the existing API, not a greenfield implementation. Deliver the five binding stories together as one capability; all workdirs are apps/api and all dependency arrays are empty. The fleet admin writes must become visible through the existing AuditEntry-backed audit log, atomically with their domain mutations, without changing HTTP contracts. This is P2 feature six of nine; audit-core and audit-fleet-routes are existing prerequisites, not stories to implement here. Codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session, so discovery used direct source reads and targeted text searches rooted at /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/koda/repos/koda. Findings below describe the inspected checkout rather than assuming the spec's baseline commit is an interface. No implementation or tests were run during PRD drafting.

ARCHITECTURE AND SHARED CONTRACT
The detected Express/Next.js labels in the prompt are not authoritative: .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:17 describes NestJS 12 + Fastify, Prisma 7 and Vitest, and apps/api/package.json:62 includes @nestjs/platform-fastify. The web app is Nuxt according to repository guidance and is untouched. Read the nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill before implementation of NestJS code. Keep business rules and persistence in apps/api; no CLI, runner, web, schema, migration, generated client or OpenAPI change is needed. apps/api/src/audit/audit-recorder.service.ts:9 defines AuditRecordInput with key, resourceType, resourceId, optional nullable projectId and optional summary; :17 defines AuditEntriesOf<T>; :31 implements audited<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>, entriesOf: AuditEntriesOf<T>): Promise<T> by running fn and recording its result-derived entries in one txManager.run. :41 implements record(input: AuditRecordInput): Promise<void>; :42 rejects unknown catalog keys and :45 rejects calls outside a transaction. :49 reads currentContext; :50 derives the actor from context, not the service's activity actorId; :54 derives origin; :56 maps missing summaries to null and caps their length. Do not manufacture actor/origin metadata in the writers or copy activity payloads into audit entries. apps/api/src/audit/prisma-audit.storage.ts:21 maps recorder fields into the stored AuditEntry, including key, resourceType, actor and summary. The package interceptor and @Audit decorator must not be introduced.

apps/api/src/audit/audit-summary.ts:2 implements fieldsSummary(patch: object): string | undefined by selecting only defined own fields and sorting their names. Use the original dto for budget and schedule updates and the existing clean patch for runner updates. Never summarize amounts, cron expressions, schedule names, labels, repo owner/name, edit content, PR titles, patterns, cutoff timestamps, confirmation strings, enrollment tokens or runner credentials. Summaries are exact contract strings built only from stored ids, field names, counts, modes, providers and scope types. Empty PATCH summary assertions are explicitly excluded. apps/api/src/audit/audit-log.module.ts:10 makes AuditLogModule global and :21 exports AuditRecorder; apps/api/src/app.module.ts:147 imports it. No fleet module needs to import AuditLogModule. apps/api/src/common/test-helpers/global-stubs.module.ts:42 exports mockAuditRecorder, whose record resolves undefined and whose audited runs fn and returns its result. Module wiring tests must remain database-free and use that global stub; route integration tests must boot the real AppModule and recorder instead. Every target constructor gets a required AuditRecorder LAST; do not make it optional.

US-001 IMPACT AND SEAMS
Modify apps/api/src/fleet/budgets/budgets.service.ts. :37 starts its constructor; create's transaction is at :59, update's at :77, remove's at :98 and resume's at :116. Extend the helper's existing actorId/action/entityType/entityId/projectId/run arguments with audit key/resourceType/resourceId/summary label. RISKS, COMPATIBILITY AND MIGRATION
The largest risks are recording outside the owning transaction (record throws), not awaiting the recorder (domain commit without audit), recording user values by reusing FleetActivity payloads, duplicate auditing of approval-driven budget resume, auditing no-op schedule toggles or zero-count queue/deletes, incorrect project scope on global entries, and queueing knowledge work before its audit succeeds. Keep forge HTTP and live/placement/drain effects outside transactions exactly as today. Do not alter FleetActivity payloads or their existing no-op rows. A recorder rejection must propagate and roll back both domain and activity changes, never be swallowed. Existing read-only/runner protocol consumers of the constructors must remain behaviorally unchanged. No new API fields, keys, permission checks, statuses, response bodies or migrations: deploy as additive writer instrumentation using the already-installed audit schema/catalog. No historical backfill is specified; historical FleetActivity rows remain separate. No story introduces symbols consumed by another, so code work can proceed independently, but shared-DB verification must be serialized. Done means the five writer groups emit the exact committed-action entries, refuse/no-op without an entry, preserve previous behavior and demonstrate rollback through real route wiring. The failure table adds an explicit unknown-job ingest 404/no-entry criterion beyond US-005's numbered twelve; all other failure rows are retained by the corresponding story criteria, including explicit recorder-failure atomicity and permission refusals.
